notes.JUICE: Melon juice can run onto the cutting board when you cut the flesh. A shallow plate can catch it when you set out a few sample pieces.

food-shops-5.solvingTip: Begin with the sliced cured meat at 11 Down. A crossing leads to what the clerk does on the scale at 10 Across.

notes.CHEESE: The deli can slice cheese thinly so it lies flat on the bread. The paper around the sandwich helps hold the cheese and other fillings in place.
notes.COUNTER: At the deli counter, you can order a sandwich and watch it being wrapped. The clerk hands the bag across the counter when the order is ready.
notes.SANDWICH: Ham and thinly sliced cheese can make up the deli sandwich on rye. A pickle can go beside it so its juice stays off the bread until lunch.

clues.CHEESE: Dairy filling often sliced thin at a deli

snacks-for-a-table.solvingTip: Find the quick sound made by a kernel opening at 4 Down. Its crossing helps you name the snack that fills the bowl at 6 Across.

notes.WHITE: When a kernel pops, the pale starch inside expands into the fluffy part you eat. Bits of the original hull may still be attached.
notes.BUTTER: Butter can be melted and poured over the popcorn after it has popped. Tossing the bowl's contents helps spread it over more of the pieces.

clues.BUTTER: Dairy topping often melted over warm popcorn

snacks-for-a-table-2.solvingTip: Try the flat serving piece that carries the cheese and crackers at 8 Down. It crosses the action of making a pile of those bite-size pieces at 10 Across.

notes.CHEESE: Cut the cheese into pieces small enough to fit on one cracker. A wedge on the tray can also be left whole for people to slice themselves.
notes.SLICE: A slice is a thin portion that can lie flat on a cracker. You can cut several slices from the wider wedge on the tray.

snacks-for-a-table-4.solvingTip: Begin at 3 Down with the soft container you carry the mix in. Its crossing at 5 Across asks for a small bite to eat between meals.

notes.SWEET: Raisins bring a sweet taste while salted nuts bring a salty one. A handful with some of each can have both flavors at once.

snacks-for-a-table-5.solvingTip: Find the word for bread after it has browned at 9 Across. At 5 Down, its crossing names the outer edge of each slice.

notes.CINNAMON: Mix a little cinnamon with sugar so the spice is spread out before it goes on the buttered toast. An even sprinkle keeps each bite from getting a clump of spice.
notes.BREAD: On a slice of bread, the cut surface becomes crisp as it toasts. The rough surface can hold the melted butter and spice mixture.
notes.KNIFE: A table knife can spread soft butter over the toast. The warm bread helps the butter melt before the cinnamon and sugar go on.

clues.CINNAMON: Brown spice often mixed with sugar for toast
clues.KNIFE: Table utensil used to spread butter on warm toast

keeping-food-fresh.solvingTip: Try the container that carries the lunch at 7 Across. One crossing leads to the utensil packed for scooping food at 5 Down.

notes.HANDLE: The handle of a lunch box carries the weight of the packed food. The lid keeps those items inside once it is fastened.
notes.FRUIT: The fruit in a packed lunch can be a whole apple. Packing it whole keeps the cut surfaces from browning before the meal.
notes.SANDWICH: A sandwich fits flat inside a lunch box and can be wrapped to keep the filling together. Placing it above heavier items helps the bread hold its shape.

clues.HANDLE: Part you grip to lift a lunch box

keeping-food-fresh-2.solvingTip: Start with the hard form water takes in the freezer at 9 Across. Its crossing helps name the action of putting one labeled container above another at 7 Down.

notes.SHELF: A freezer shelf supports containers as they stack. Put the dates where you can read them from the front, even after another box goes on top.
notes.LABEL: A freezer label tells you what is inside a closed container. A dry spot on the side or lid gives adhesive tape a surface it can stick to before freezing.

clues.SHELF: Flat surface inside a freezer that supports containers
clues.LABEL: Tag showing what food is inside a freezer container

keeping-food-fresh-3.solvingTip: Find the part you open before putting groceries away at 2 Down. It crosses the everyday name for the whole appliance at 6 Across.

clues.DOOR: Part you swing open to reach the chilled shelves
clues.DRAWER: Pull-out section of the refrigerator for produce
clues.BUTTER: Refrigerated dairy spread made from cream

notes.DRAWER: Pulling the drawer out gives you room to reach produce. It sits below the shelves where bottles and jars can stand.
notes.CHEESE: Putting the cheese back in its wrapper after opening keeps the exposed edge from drying out as quickly. The wrapped piece can go on a shelf with the other chilled food.
notes.BUTTER: Keeping butter wrapped in the fridge helps protect it from the smells of other foods. The wrapper also keeps its exposed surface from drying out too quickly.

keeping-food-fresh-5.solvingTip: Look first for the cover that closes the breadbox at 1 Across. Its crossing names the whole baked bread inside at 1 Down.

clues.CRUMB: Small loose bit that falls from a slice of bread
clues.COUNTER: Kitchen surface a breadbox can sit on

notes.COUNTER: A breadbox can sit on the counter within reach when you make a sandwich. Its lid covers the loaf, while the counter leaves you a flat place to cut a slice.
notes.BREAD: A covered breadbox helps keep the bread from drying out in the open air. If a loaf has been cut, its exposed end can be tucked into a bag before the lid is closed.
notes.CRUST: A loaf's crust is darker and firmer than its crumb, the soft inside revealed when it is sliced. A crisp crust can soften after the loaf sits in a breadbox.

neighborhood-businesses.solvingTip: Look at 10 Across for the small metal piece that fits a lock. One of its letters helps you name the device that cuts a copy at 4 Down.

clues.MACHINE: Device at the hardware store that cuts a copy of a house key
clues.COUNTER: Raised surface where you give the worker a key to copy

notes.METAL: The worker starts with a plain metal blank. Cutting its edge makes the shape that fits the lock.
notes.COUNTER: The counter is where you hand the original key to the hardware worker. The cutting machine can sit behind it on the worker's side.

neighborhood-businesses-2.solvingTip: Try 9 Across for the tool you use to sign the card in ink. Its crossing belongs to the friendly words inside at 4 Down.

notes.PRICE: The price of a greeting card can be printed on the back. Look separately for the envelope in the rack behind the cards.
notes.ENVELOPE: A greeting card needs an envelope wide enough for its fold and corners. Cards on a shop rack often have a matching one tucked behind them.
notes.THANKS: A shop card can carry a printed message of thanks. The blank space inside gives you room to add a short greeting in your own words.

clues.ENVELOPE: Paper holder that fits around a greeting card

neighborhood-businesses-3.solvingTip: Start with the container the parcel goes in at 9 Across. At 7 Down, look for the more specific word for a container made of stiff cardboard.

clues.CARTON: Stiff cardboard container suitable for shipping
clues.BOX: Container you fill before sealing a parcel
clues.COUNTER: Flat surface where a clerk takes a package for shipping
clues.RECEIPT: Record of the shipping charge that may show a tracking number

notes.COUNTER: The shipping counter gives you a flat spot to set down the parcel. The clerk can move it from there to the scale before making the label.
notes.RECEIPT: A shipping receipt may show a tracking number along with the charge. The destination address travels on the parcel's own label.

neighborhood-businesses-4.solvingTip: Find the clear piece that sits in front of one eye at 10 Across. Then use the crossing to name the holder that protects the glasses at 8 Down.

clues.LENS: Clear curved piece you look through in a pair of glasses

neighborhood-businesses-5.solvingTip: Try the metal container you open and stir at 12 Across. The crossing at 10 Down asks for the shallow place where you pour a little paint for the roller.

clues.TRAY: Shallow holder you pour paint into for a roller
clues.COLOR: Quality that distinguishes blue paint from green paint

notes.BRUSH: A brush can reach the narrow edge of a wall. A wide roller covers the open surface more quickly.
notes.COLOR: A swatch shows the color of paint. Gloss tells you how shiny the dried surface will look. Two cans can have the same color with different finishes.
notes.PAINT: Paint can look a little different on a wall than it does on a small store swatch. A dry sample lets you see how that coating looks in the room's light.

around-the-town-square.solvingTip: Begin with what you carry the apples home in at 5 Across. It crosses the place the produce was grown at 3 Down.

notes.PRICE: A market sign might list apples by the pound and corn by the ear. The amount named beside each price tells you what that price will buy.
notes.APPLE: At a market stall, two kinds of apple can look alike in their crates. A sign with the variety name can help you recognize the kind you meant to buy.

clues.APPLE: Round orchard fruit a market may sell by the pound

around-the-town-square-2.solvingTip: What time is halfway through the day? Try 6 Across, then use its crossing to name the device on the tower at 3 Down.

clues.HAND: Pointer that moves around the face of the town clock

notes.CLOCK: At noon, the hour pointer reaches twelve and the minute pointer comes back to the same mark. The chime can announce the hour to people below.

around-the-town-square-3.solvingTip: Look for the cloth symbol that moves in the breeze at 3 Across. One crossing leads to the room where neighbors gather at 1 Down.

notes.FLOWER: The flower is the part of the bedding plant that blooms. Planting several colors together gives people something to see on the way into the building.
notes.WINDOW: The front windows look out over the flower beds at the town hall. The beds frame the view at ground level, while the flag stands higher up.

around-the-town-square-4.solvingTip: Start with the small fastener pressed into the notice board at 4 Down. Its crossing names the kind of gathering the notice might announce at 6 Across.

clues.BOARD: Flat surface where local notices are put up
clues.PHOTO: Picture taken with a camera and pinned beside a notice

notes.GLASS: The glass front protects the pinned announcements. You can read the date through it even when the board's cover is closed.
notes.PHOTO: A photo pinned beside a notice can show what happened at an earlier event. The date on the notice tells when a future event will take place.

around-the-town-square-5.solvingTip: Picture what someone tosses when making a wish at 1 Down. It shares a square with the broad bowl that catches the fountain water at 6 Across.

notes.WATER: A recirculating fountain lifts water to the spout and catches it again in the basin. A coin dropped in usually settles at the bottom.

visits-and-gatherings-2.solvingTip: Try the word for a warm embrace at 9 Across. Then use its crossing to name the picture the family takes together at 8 Down.

notes.TABLE: A picnic table gives relatives a shared place to set out food. A separate corner can hold family photos where people can stop to look at them.
notes.FAMILY: A family reunion can bring together relatives from several households. A cousin, an aunt, and an uncle can all be part of the same gathering.
notes.PHOTO: One reunion photo can show relatives from several households together. Taking it before people begin to leave gives more of the group a chance to be in it.

clues.PHOTO: Picture taken with a camera of relatives at a reunion

visits-and-gatherings-3.solvingTip: Start at 7 Down with the word for a friendly, informal talk. Its crossing helps with the name for the place where people meet at 7 Across.

clues.CENTER: Place with rooms for classes, games, and other group activities

visits-and-gatherings-4.solvingTip: Find the little label attached to an item at 3 Across. It shares a square with the name of the event where neighbors buy the items at 1 Down.

notes.TABLE: At a yard sale, a table brings small items up where people can look at them easily. A price tag can stay with an item when a shopper picks it up.
notes.PRICE: A tag carries the asking price as a shopper picks up a yard-sale item. When a seller agrees to a bargain, the amount paid can be lower than the tag.

clues.TABLE: Raised surface where yard-sale items are set out

visits-and-gatherings-5.solvingTip: Look at 9 Down for what helps the newcomers find their way around. A crossing leads to what they might use to wash their hands at 10 Across.

notes.BASKET: The basket keeps small welcome gifts together at the door. A neighborhood map or note can go on top so it is easy to spot.
notes.RIBBON: A ribbon across the basket can hold a welcome card in view. The towels and other useful gifts can be packed below it.

clues.BASKET: Handled container for holding welcome gifts

household-paperwork.solvingTip: Start with the little stack of sheets you pull toward you at 1 Across. Its crossing asks what those sheets are made of at 1 Down.

clues.PAD: Small stack of writing sheets joined at one edge
clues.PENCIL: Erasable writing tool for making a grocery list

notes.PAPER: A writing pad keeps the sheets together while you add items. You can tear one loose to take it to the store.
notes.PENCIL: A pencil lets you change the grocery list as you check what is already in the cupboard. It also lets you cross out items as they go into the cart.

household-paperwork-2.solvingTip: Find the ink-writing tool at 2 Down. One crossing helps name the signed payment you put into the envelope at 3 Across.

clues.SEAL: Press the envelope flap down so it stays shut
clues.ENVELOPE: Paper holder used to mail a signed payment

notes.ENVELOPE: A bill can come with a return envelope for the payment. Its printed address shows where the signed check is meant to go.
notes.STAMP: A stamp pays postage on the bill's return envelope. Some reply envelopes already have a printed postage marking, so the front can show whether a stamp is needed.

household-paperwork-3.solvingTip: Try the short word for a single square on the calendar at 3 Across. It crosses the span of all twelve months at 4 Down.

household-paperwork-4.solvingTip: Start with the letters and envelopes that arrive together at 4 Across. Its crossing names where you spread them out to sort them at 1 Down.

notes.ENVELOPE: An unopened envelope can keep a bill and any inserts in one place until you are ready to sort them. The sender printed on the outside can help you decide which pile it belongs in.
notes.LETTER: A personal letter can be put aside to read after you sort the bills. Keeping it with its envelope can preserve the sender's return address.
notes.STAMP: A stamp can stick to the outside of an envelope among the morning mail. A postmark may run over it and show where or when the letter was handled.

clues.LETTER: Personal message on paper that may arrive with the morning mail

household-paperwork-5.solvingTip: Look for the little label that sticks up above a folder at 10 Across. It crosses the action of putting similar papers together at 8 Down.

notes.PAPER: Put each loose paper into a folder with the right subject. The tab at the top can still be read when the papers themselves are out of sight.
notes.LABEL: A few words on a folder label can describe a group of papers at a glance. Keep related labels together so it is easy to see where a new page belongs.

clues.PAPER: Sheet material you put into a file folder
clues.LABEL: Tag showing what kind of papers are in a folder

fresh-laundry.solvingTip: Try the short name for a fastener that holds a shirt up to dry at 12 Down. Its crossing helps you name the cord stretched between the poles at 11 Across.

clues.PIN: Fasten wet fabric to the line with a clip
clues.SHEET: Large piece of bedding that can hang from a clothesline

notes.SHEET: A wet sheet can be hung with its corners spread along the line. Pegs keep the cloth in place while air can move along its surface.
notes.POLE: The pole holds the clothesline up off the grass. It keeps a long sheet from brushing the ground as the cloth hangs down to dry.

fresh-laundry-2.solvingTip: Begin with what you do when you bring the fabric edges together at 3 Down. A crossing leads to the cloth you put on the shelf at 4 Across.

clues.TOWEL: Absorbent cloth folded and put away after drying
clues.COTTON: Plant fiber often used in absorbent bath towels
clues.CORNER: Point where two edges of a towel meet

notes.SHELF: A shelf gives the folded towels a flat place to rest. Stacking them with the folds facing forward makes each towel easier to pick out.
notes.COTTON: Cotton loops help a bath towel take up water. After the towel is dry, folding the edges inward makes a neat stack on the shelf.
notes.CORNER: Match two corners of a towel before smoothing the fold across it. Lining up the corners keeps one layer from sticking out beyond the rest.

fresh-laundry-3.solvingTip: Find the garment that comes in a pair and goes inside a shoe at 2 Down. Its crossing helps name the container the clean laundry came out of at 6 Across.

clues.CUFF: Band at the top of a sock

notes.BASKET: A laundry basket can hold socks while you look for matches. Set a completed pair to one side so it stays together while you sort the rest.
notes.COTTON: Cotton is one fiber used to make socks. Since several pairs may be made from the same fiber, a stripe or a patterned cuff can help you find the match.
notes.DRAWER: A drawer can hold stacks or rows of paired socks. Put the ones still waiting for a match at one end so they are easy to find after the next wash.

fresh-laundry-4.solvingTip: Look for the heated tool that removes wrinkles at 7 Down. Its crossing names the action you take as you lower the tool onto the cloth at 9 Across.

clues.CORD: Covered wire that carries power from the outlet to the iron
clues.TABLE: Piece of furniture you can cover with a cloth before dinner

notes.TABLE: The dining table is what the cloth will cover. Iron the cloth on an ironing board, then check how evenly it hangs over the table's edges.
notes.COTTON: A cotton tablecloth can crease along the lines where it was folded. Use the fabric setting that matches the care label when pressing those lines out.

fresh-laundry-5.solvingTip: Start with what cleans the sweater in the basin at 3 Across. Then try the crossing for the part that covers an arm at 3 Down.

clues.SLEEVE: Part of a sweater covering an arm
clues.SINK: Basin where the sweater is soaked and rinsed
clues.WATER: Clear liquid that carries soap out of a rinsed sweater

notes.TOWEL: A towel laid flat can take up some of the moisture from a washed sweater. The basin is where the earlier soaking and rinsing happen.
notes.WATER: Rinsing a hand-washed sweater in fresh water carries away soap left in the fibers. A towel can take up extra moisture before you lay the sweater flat.

home-cleaning-corners.solvingTip: Think of the little vessel you drink from at 11 Down. It crosses the frame you set it on after rinsing at 10 Across.

clues.RACK: Frame where washed dishes are set to dry

notes.WATER: The soapy water helps loosen food from a dish. Rinsing uses fresh water to carry off the soap before the dish goes onto the rack.
notes.PLATE: A plate can stand on its edge between two bars of the rack. That lets the rinse water run off instead of collecting on the surface.

home-cleaning-corners-2.solvingTip: Try the fine dirt you wipe away at 6 Across. Its crossing names the flat place you lift the books from before wiping at 7 Down.

notes.SHELF: Dust can collect on the shelf under a frame or vase. Lifting one item at a time lets you wipe the area it was covering.
notes.FEATHER: Soft feathers can form the head of a duster. They can reach into the space behind the books or around the edges of a frame.

clues.FEATHER: Light bird covering used to make some dusters

home-cleaning-corners-3.solvingTip: At 5 Across, find the thing you sweep the grit into. Use a crossing for the place where two edges of the steps meet at 2 Down.

clues.PAN: Shallow scoop you sweep dust and leaves into
clues.PORCH: Level entrance platform at the top of the front steps
clues.CORNER: Place where two sides of a step meet

notes.HANDLE: A long broom handle lets you reach the step below you. The bristles at the far end bend and pull loose leaves along the surface.
notes.PORCH: The porch floor is the level surface at the top of the steps. Loose leaves can be swept away from the corners before you work down the steps.
notes.CORNER: Dirt can collect in the corner where a step meets a side wall. The end of the broom can draw that debris out into the open.

home-cleaning-corners-4.solvingTip: Find the basin beneath the mirror at 4 Across. At 1 Down, its crossing asks what the mirror does when it reflects light after cleaning.

clues.FRAME: Rigid border holding the mirror glass
clues.SINK: Basin beneath the mirror where water drains away
clues.GLASS: Smooth clear surface you wipe on the front of a mirror

notes.FRAME: The frame supports the glass at its edges. A separate mounting bracket may help hold the mirror against the wall.
notes.GLASS: The glass is the front surface you wipe. A layer behind it reflects the image, so a spot on the front can still interrupt what you see.

home-cleaning-corners-5.solvingTip: Try the piece of furniture you make up at 9 Across. Its crossing points to the large piece of cloth you tuck around the mattress at 8 Down.

notes.SHEET: A fitted sheet stretches around the corners of the mattress. A flat sheet lies above it and can be tucked along the bottom of the bed.
notes.BLANKET: The blanket goes on above the sheet. Straightening it across the bed gives it a similar amount of overhang on both sides.

useful-home-repairs.solvingTip: Start with the round part you turn to open the door at 3 Across. It crosses the condition that makes the handle wobble at 2 Down.

clues.LATCH: Small fastening that keeps a door shut

notes.HANDLE: The handle is what you hold to open the door. The nearby screw secures it, and the latch is the part that holds the door closed.

useful-home-repairs-2.solvingTip: Look at 1 Down for the small metal fastener that goes into the wall. A crossing helps with the tool that strikes it at 3 Across.

notes.GLASS: The clear pane in the frame protects the picture. When you use a level to straighten the frame, rest it on the wooden edge.
notes.PENCIL: Use a pencil to make a small mark where the picture hook will go. A light mark can be erased if the place changes after measuring.

clues.PENCIL: Writing tool used to mark a spot for a picture hook

useful-home-repairs-3.solvingTip: Try the part that lights up inside the lamp at 6 Down. Its crossing names the part that rests on the table at 6 Across.

clues.SHADE: Cover around a lamp that softens its glare
clues.BULB: Part of a lamp that gives off light
clues.CLIP: Small fastener that holds the lamp covering in place
clues.TABLE: Piece of furniture that a small lamp rests on

notes.SHADE: The shade covers the brightest part of the lamp. It can spread the light or direct more of it toward the table.
notes.TABLE: A table lamp has a base that rests on a piece of furniture. Its shade fits higher up, around the bulb.
notes.LIGHT: The bulb gives off the light. A fabric shade can soften its glare and let more light fall through the openings at the top and bottom.

useful-home-repairs-4.solvingTip: Find the liquid that helps a squeaky hinge move smoothly at 6 Across. Then look for what you do to shut the cabinet at 4 Down.

clues.OIL: Slippery liquid used to quiet a squeaky hinge

at-the-writing-desk.solvingTip: Find what you hold to make ink marks at 10 Across. Its crossing at 7 Down names the action of putting words on the page.

clues.WRITE: Put the words of a message on paper
clues.LETTER: Written message that can share news with a grandchild

notes.PAPER: Your note goes on the paper, and the address goes on the envelope. Leave room at the end of the last page for the closing and your name.
notes.ENVELOPE: Fold the pages of the letter together so they fit inside one envelope. If there are several pages, a page number helps your grandchild read them in order.
notes.LETTER: A letter to a grandchild can include a small piece of family news or a question for the next reply. Dating the first page gives the reader a time to remember it by.

at-the-writing-desk-2.solvingTip: Look at 1 Down for the three-letter word before code in a mailing address. A crossing helps with the other kind of number in the book at 4 Across.

clues.LETTER: One alphabet symbol used to group names in an address book

notes.LETTER: An address book can have one section for each initial. Search under the first letter of a last name to find the entry.

at-the-writing-desk-3.solvingTip: Begin with the everyday name for the pencil's dark center at 2 Across. Its crossing names the rubber piece used to remove a mark at 3 Down.

notes.PENCIL: Sharpening a wooden pencil exposes more of the writing core. A point with a little graphite showing can make small letters easier to fit inside a crossword square.

at-the-writing-desk-4.solvingTip: Try the small stack of sheets used for jottings at 9 Down. It crosses the compartment you pull open to reach the supplies at 11 Across.

clues.PAD: Small block of paper for jotting things down
clues.PIN: Short pointed fastener you press into a notice board
clues.DRAWER: Pull-out desk compartment that can hold clips and pens

notes.DRAWER: The drawer keeps small supplies close to the desk surface. A shallow box inside it can keep clips and pins from mixing with the pens.

at-the-writing-desk-5.solvingTip: Look for the short message you are writing at 8 Down. At 10 Across, its crossing asks for what you sign at the bottom.

notes.PAPER: A folded sheet gives you an inside surface for the thank-you message. Naming the gift or the kind act makes the short note more personal.
notes.ENVELOPE: A small thank-you card can fit into an envelope without another fold. The flap closes over the card so its message stays private while it travels.
notes.THANKS: Many thanks is a familiar way to close a handwritten note. It can go on the line above your signature.

clues.PAPER: Sheet material you write a thank-you note on

through-the-front-door.solvingTip: Find the wet dirt you brush off before coming in at 9 Across. Its crossing helps you spell the name of the rug beside the threshold at 5 Down.

clues.MUD: Wet dirt you wipe off your boots at the door
clues.PORCH: Area just outside the front door where visitors can wipe their feet
clues.BRUSH: Bristled tool for cleaning dried mud from boots

notes.PORCH: The porch gives visitors a place to stop before crossing the threshold. A mat there catches some of the dirt from their boots.
notes.BRUSH: A stiff brush can loosen dried mud from a boot before you use the doormat. Short bristles can reach the grooves in the sole.

through-the-front-door-2.solvingTip: Try the thin support that holds the umbrella open at 8 Across. Then look for what drips off when you bring it inside at 4 Down.

clues.WATER: Liquid dripping from the wet umbrella

notes.WATER: A stand gives the dripping umbrella a place to rest. Some stands have a tray at the bottom to catch the drops.
notes.HANDLE: When you set an umbrella in a stand, the handle stays near the top. The wet fabric below can drip into the stand instead of onto the floor.

through-the-front-door-3.solvingTip: Start with the outer garment you take off indoors at 4 Down. Its crossing points to the curved piece on the wall at 5 Across.

clues.HOOK: Curved piece on the wall to hang an outdoor coat on

notes.HOOK: A hook bears the weight of a coat from its loop. A hanger holds the garment across both shoulders.

through-the-front-door-4.solvingTip: Look at 9 Across for the metal piece shaped to open the lock. A crossing helps with the word for the extra one set aside at 5 Down.

notes.HOUSE: A house key usually belongs to one of the building's doors. A spare hung in a familiar place can be found without sorting through a whole key ring.

clues.HOUSE: Building you unlock before coming home

through-the-front-door-5.solvingTip: Find what holds the cut flowers at 8 Down. One crossing leads to the piece of furniture it rests on at 10 Across.

notes.DRAWER: A small drawer in the entry table can hold spare items such as a key or a pen. The top of the table stays clear for the lamp and things you pick up daily.
notes.PHOTO: A photo on the entry table can show a person or place you recognize when you come in the door. A small stand behind its frame keeps the picture upright.

restful-household-routines.solvingTip: Begin with the control you turn to fill the tub at 2 Down. It shares a square with what makes a lather at 5 Across.

restful-household-routines-2.solvingTip: Try the word for opening your mouth when sleepy at 1 Down. Its crossing names the dark hours when you go to sleep at 5 Across.

notes.NIGHT: Here night is the part of the day set aside for winding down. The bedside book and pillow are part of that routine.
notes.SHEET: The sheet is the light layer on the bed just below a blanket. Pulling that layer smooth can make it easier to slide into bed.

restful-household-routines-3.solvingTip: Look for the place you lie down to sleep at 9 Across. A crossing leads to the piece of furniture beside it at 6 Down.

notes.WATER: The water in this scene is the drink beside the bed. A glass on the table is easy to reach for a sip without getting up.
notes.GLASS: The glass is the vessel on the bedside table. Clear sides let you see how much water is left without picking it up.
notes.DRAWER: A nightstand drawer keeps small belongings below the tabletop. That leaves the glass of water and the book within reach above it.

clues.WATER: Clear drink in the glass beside the bed
clues.GLASS: Small drinking vessel on the nightstand
clues.DRAWER: Pull-out compartment in a bedside table

restful-household-routines-5.solvingTip: Find the drawing that shows the roads at 9 Down. Its crossing names the drink you pack in a bottle at 10 Across.

clues.WATER: Clear drink carried in a bottle on a day out

notes.WATER: Water travels in a bottle in the day bag. Closing the bottle securely helps keep stray drops away from the tissues and map.
notes.HANDLE: A day bag's handle is the part you lift it by. A pocket keeps small items within reach, and the zipper closes the opening.

on-the-local-road.solvingTip: Try the action of coming to a halt at 4 Down. It crosses the part of the signal that shows when to do it at 5 Across.

clues.LIGHT: Signal that changes color to tell cars when to stop

on-the-local-road-2.solvingTip: Look at 8 Across for what goes in the parking space. Its crossing names the device that tracks the paid time at 6 Down.

clues.TICKET: Printed slip showing payment or a parking violation
clues.METER: Device beside a parking space that records paid time

notes.STRING: Wrapping string around the top lets a quick pull turn the toy. It then balances for a short time on its point.

remembering-simple-play-5.solvingTip: Try the small vessel that stands in front of a doll at 9 Across. A crossing helps name the bigger vessel with a spout at 8 Down.

notes.BASKET: A small basket can hold toy cups while you carry them to the checkered blanket. The blanket becomes the place to set out the pretend meal.
notes.PLATE: The picnic plate is small enough for a doll's meal. Set it on the blanket with the toy cups to make a place setting.
notes.BLANKET: A small checkered blanket gives the doll picnic an outline on the ground. Its squares can help separate the cups from the plates in the pretend place settings.

clues.BASKET: Small carrying container for toy cups
clues.PLATE: Small flat dish for a doll's pretend lunch
clues.BLANKET: Small cloth spread out for a doll's pretend picnic

winter-indoor-afternoons.solvingTip: Picture what you open to read a story at 6 Down. Its crossing names what you pull over your lap to stay warm at 6 Across.

notes.WINDOW: The window is where you can see snow falling from inside the room. A nearby lamp still gives you enough light to read when the daylight fades.
notes.BLANKET: A blanket keeps your lap covered while you hold the book above it. The top edge can be folded down so your hands stay free to turn a page.

winter-indoor-afternoons-2.solvingTip: Start with the drink you make by steeping leaves at 1 Down. It crosses the warm vapor that rises from the kettle at 2 Across.

clues.SPOUT: Shaped opening that guides hot water out of a kettle

notes.WATER: When the kettle boils, some of the water turns to steam. In a whistling kettle, the escaping steam makes the whistle sound.
notes.WINTER: In a cool kitchen in winter, the cloud above the kettle can be easy to see. It forms as vapor cools into tiny drops in the air.

winter-indoor-afternoons-3.solvingTip: Look for the container that holds soil by the window at 6 Across. Its crossing describes a flower stem that reaches high above the soil at 7 Down.

clues.BULB: Round plant base that sends up the flower stalk
clues.FLOWER: Bloom near the top of an amaryllis stalk
clues.WINTER: Cold season when an indoor amaryllis can bloom in January

notes.WATER: The amaryllis bulb stores what it needs to begin growing. After growth starts, water in the potting mix helps support the rising stalk and opening flowers.
notes.FLOWER: An amaryllis grows a tall stalk from its bulb. More than one flower can open near the top of that stalk.
notes.WINTER: A potted amaryllis can bloom indoors during winter. It can bring color to a windowsill while outdoor beds are still quiet.

winter-indoor-afternoons-4.solvingTip: Try the short action that puts a puzzle piece into the space shaped for it at 3 Down. Its crossing names the heater beside the table at 6 Across.

notes.WINTER: A winter afternoon can be spent at the puzzle table near the radiator. An empty corner of the table gives you room to sort pieces with straight edges.
notes.CHAIR: At a puzzle table, the chair can be moved to the edge you are working on. Keep the box where you can still see the picture when you change places.
notes.CORNER: On a rectangular jigsaw, a corner piece has two flat sides that meet at a right angle. Look for the four pieces with that shape to mark the outside corners.

clues.CORNER: Part of a jigsaw border where two straight sides meet

winter-indoor-afternoons-5.solvingTip: Find the band at the end of a sleeve at 1 Across. One crossing gives you a letter for the soft fiber the shirt may be made from at 1 Down.

notes.COTTON: Flannel can be made from cotton. Brushing the surface raises fine fibers and gives the shirt a soft feel.

clues.COTTON: Plant fiber used to make many flannel shirts

winter-in-the-neighborhood.solvingTip: Look for the footwear you pull on before walking in snow at 7 Down. Its crossing names the part underneath that leaves a mark at 10 Across.

notes.WHITE: On fresh white snow, the different depths of a boot print make its tread pattern visible. A light dusting later can soften the edges of those marks.

winter-in-the-neighborhood-2.solvingTip: Find the body part suggested by a stick at the snowman's side at 3 Across. Its crossing describes the shape of the packed snow at 4 Down.

clues.ARM: Part of a snowman made with a stick at its side

notes.WHITE: The body of a snowman usually keeps the white color of the packed snow. A dark button shows up well on that background.
notes.WINTER: The snowman keeps its shape while the weather stays cold. A scarf can lend it some color before a warm stretch of winter weather softens the snow.

winter-in-the-neighborhood-3.solvingTip: Begin with what holds the mailbox up from the ground at 1 Across. Its crossing leads to the place you shovel clear so people can walk up at 1 Down.

clues.BANK: Long mound of snow piled beside the road
clues.PATH: Route cleared for walking to the mailbox
clues.POST: Upright piece that holds the mailbox above the ground
clues.LETTER: Written message delivered to a mailbox

notes.BANK: Clearing the walk or road can leave a ridge of snow along its edge. Here, that ridge is near the mailbox.
notes.WHITE: White snow on the ground can partly hide the edge of a driveway. A dark mailbox or post makes a useful marker when you clear the path.
notes.LETTER: The letter is the piece of mail that goes inside the box on the post. A clear path to the box makes it easier to pick up the mail after a snowfall.

winter-in-the-neighborhood-4.solvingTip: Try the word for the place selling the gifts at 10 Across. At 5 Down, its crossing names the clear material you look through to see the display.

notes.WINTER: When daylight ends early in winter, lit shop windows stand out from the street. You can see the toys and gifts from outside after the shops close.
notes.WINDOW: A shop puts its holiday display behind the front window. People on the sidewalk can see the lit toys and gifts even when the door is closed.

clues.WINTER: Season of cold evenings and many holiday window displays
clues.WINDOW: Glass-fronted opening where a shop displays gifts

winter-in-the-neighborhood-5.solvingTip: Look for what keeps your head warm at 1 Across. Its crossing names the curved support it can hang from after you come inside at 1 Down.

notes.WINTER: Hang the hat and mittens where air can reach them after a winter outing. Set the pair together so both mittens are there the next time you go out.

winter-light-and-ice.solvingTip: Find the short word for water in its hard, frozen form at 11 Across. A crossing leads to the season when you may see it on the porch roof at 7 Down.

clues.POINT: Narrow end of an icicle farthest from the roof
clues.WINTER: Cold season when icicles may hang from a roof

notes.POINT: The broad end is nearest the roof. The thin end hangs below it and may drip when the air warms.
notes.WINTER: On a winter day, sun can melt snow on the roof. An icicle can grow when some of that runoff freezes again at the colder edge.

winter-light-and-ice-2.solvingTip: Try the word for one flat piece of window glass at 6 Down. Then use its crossing to name the repeated design that frost leaves on the glass at 6 Across.

clues.FEATHER: Bird covering whose shape a frost pattern can resemble

notes.FEATHER: As the ice grows, small branches can reach outward from a central line. The pattern may look like part of a bird's feather.
notes.WINTER: In winter a window can get cold enough for moisture to form ice crystals on the pane. As the crystals spread they can make patterns like feathers.

winter-light-and-ice-3.solvingTip: Look for the little string that feeds the flame at 9 Down. Its crossing names the season when afternoon light fades early at 10 Across.

notes.WINTER: Winter daylight can fade while it is still afternoon. A nearby candle gives a small warm glow and can cast moving shadows as the flame flickers.

winter-light-and-ice-4.solvingTip: Find the source of light above the street at 5 Across. One crossing helps with the word for a single piece of snow that catches that light at 3 Down.

clues.LAMP: Light fixture high above the street

notes.LAMP: A streetlamp lights just part of the air around it. Falling flakes may brighten as they pass through that spot.
notes.LIGHT: The streetlamp illuminates a small part of the street. A flake can glow briefly as it passes through that patch of light.
notes.WINTER: Under a streetlamp, winter snow can seem to appear as it enters the beam. Flakes outside that bright patch are much harder to see.

winter-light-and-ice-5.solvingTip: Start with the narrow walking route at 3 Across. Its crossing points to the little pool beside it with a frozen surface at 3 Down.

notes.WATER: The top of a shallow puddle can freeze while water below remains liquid. The first layer at the surface is the thin ice described in the puzzle.
notes.WINTER: A winter puddle may stay frozen longer in the shade. The thin ice can start to melt in parts of the path that get afternoon sun.

clues.WATER: Liquid that freezes to make the top of a puddle
clues.WINTER: Cold season when puddles can freeze over

christmas-sharing-projects.solvingTip: Try the small label that carries a wish at 2 Down. Its crossing leads to the short word for a plaything someone might donate at 2 Across.

notes.RIBBON: A ribbon can decorate the wrapped present. The tag carries the requested gift information, so place it where it stays visible.
notes.CHRISTMAS: An Angel Tree is one way people organize Christmas gift donations. The tag can give details that help a shopper choose a requested gift.

christmas-sharing-projects-2.solvingTip: Find the metal container that keeps the cookies together at 4 Across. It crosses the word for something given to a friend at 3 Down.

notes.RIBBON: Tie the ribbon around the closed tin to dress it up as a gift. The paper inside separates layers of cookies.
notes.CHRISTMAS: Cookies packed in a tin are easy to share at Christmas. The liner between layers helps keep the tops of the cookies tidy until the tin is opened.

clues.RIBBON: Decorative strip tied around a gift tin

christmas-sharing-projects-3.solvingTip: Try the tool that puts ink on the envelope at 4 Down. A crossing helps name the little piece of postage added before mailing it at 2 Across.

notes.ENVELOPE: Compare the name on each Christmas card with the name on its envelope before sealing it. That helps the personal greeting reach the person you wrote it for.
notes.STAMP: Putting a stamp on each addressed envelope is one of the last steps before mailing Christmas cards. A check mark on the list can show which ones are ready.

clues.ENVELOPE: Folded paper holder used to send a holiday card
clues.STAMP: Postage label you put on a Christmas card's envelope

christmas-sharing-projects-4.solvingTip: Look at 8 Across for the part of a carol you could hum. Its crossing names the single piece of paper people read the words from at 7 Down.

notes.CHRISTMAS: At a Christmas sing-along, a printed carol sheet gives everyone the same words. A pianist can start the tune while guests find the first line.
notes.SHEET: One printed sheet can carry several verses of a carol. A clear title at the top helps guests find the right words before the singing begins.
notes.PIANO: A pianist can give a singer the starting note and keep time as the carol continues. People following a printed sheet can join in once they recognize the tune.

clues.SHEET: Piece of paper printed with the words to sing

christmas-sharing-projects-5.solvingTip: Try what holds one piece of paper to another at 4 Down. Its crossing names the tiny bits that catch the light on a decoration at 4 Across.

notes.TABLE: The craft table gives each person room to make something. Shared scissors or glue can sit in the center where several people can reach them.
notes.PAPER: Thin paper folds easily into a small ornament. A heavier sheet gives a greeting card enough stiffness to stand when folded in half.
notes.RIBBON: On a handmade decoration, a short ribbon loop can also be the hanger. A strip set flat on a card can mark a border.

clues.TABLE: Raised surface where friends set out craft supplies

christmas-little-traditions.solvingTip: Find the front part of the stocking at 9 Down, where a small treat might settle. It crosses the name of the holiday at 8 Across.

notes.FRUIT: An orange is a piece of fruit that fits in the toe of a stocking. Its peel keeps the sections inside until someone is ready to eat it.
notes.CHRISTMAS: An orange can nestle at the bottom of a Christmas stocking because the toe widens there. Small nuts or wrapped treats can fit in the space above it.

christmas-little-traditions-2.solvingTip: Look for one metal bar the toy wheels run along at 2 Down. Its crossing helps name what goes around the tree at 3 Across.

clues.RAIL: One metal bar that the wheels of the model train run along
clues.WHEEL: Round part that rolls along a toy train track
clues.TREE: Evergreen with a trunk and branches that can be decorated for Christmas

notes.CHRISTMAS: A toy train set at Christmas can make a loop around the base of the tree. From the front, you may see the engine disappear behind the trunk and come back into view.
notes.WHEEL: Small wheels support the toy engine and cars on the rails. On a curved track, those wheels follow the rails around the tree.
notes.TREE: An evergreen Christmas tree has needles along its branches. If it is a cut tree, a stand at the base holds the trunk upright.

christmas-little-traditions-3.solvingTip: Start with the wavy bend in a piece of candy at 4 Down. Then use its crossing to name the holiday when this candy often appears at 4 Across.

notes.SWEET: Ribbon candy is bent into curves while it is warm and pliable. After it hardens, its sweet taste remains in each thin fold.
notes.RIBBON: In ribbon candy, ribbon describes the shape of a thin strip of sugar candy. The strip is bent into folds before it cools and hardens.
notes.CHRISTMAS: Ribbon candy is often set out at Christmas in several bright colors. A shallow bowl lets more of the thin curls show, since the pieces can be fragile when piled up.

clues.RIBBON: Long, flat strip whose shape a folded Christmas candy copies

christmas-little-traditions-4.solvingTip: Try the little object that rings when the door moves at 9 Across. Its crossing names the light ringing sound you hear at 3 Down.

notes.HANDLE: Tying the bell's ribbon around the door handle makes it ring when the door moves. The ribbon holds the bell above the floor.
notes.RIBBON: A ribbon loop suspends the bell from the door handle. When the door moves, the hanging bell can swing and ring.

clues.HANDLE: Part of the door you hold to open it

christmas-little-traditions-5.solvingTip: Look at 10 Across for the paper item you wear on your head. Its crossing at 8 Down asks for the word for a little present.

clues.CRACKER: Paper table favor that makes a snap when pulled apart
clues.CHRISTMAS: December holiday when people may pull paper crackers at dinner

notes.PAPER: In this holiday custom, people pull on the ends of a paper cracker. Inside there may be a folded hat, a joke, or a small toy.
notes.PLATE: In a Christmas place setting, a cracker can sit beside the dinner plate. The cracker opens to reveal the folded paper crown.
notes.CHRISTMAS: Pulling crackers at Christmas dinner is especially familiar in Britain. A meal with paper crowns on the guests can be a sign that the crackers have already been pulled.

christmas-preparing-the-room.solvingTip: Try the green part beside a holly berry at 2 Down. It crosses the wax decoration that gives light to the table at 1 Across.

notes.PLATE: The plates go in front of the diners along the sides of the table. The holly and runner are in the middle, where they leave the place settings clear.
notes.CHRISTMAS: Holly gives the Christmas table a mix of green leaves and red berries. The narrow runner brings those colors down the center between the place settings.

clues.PLATE: Dish set in front of each diner on the decorated table

christmas-preparing-the-room-2.solvingTip: Find what you do with ribbon to secure it at 8 Down. A crossing helps name one thin green part of an evergreen branch at 9 Across.

notes.BRANCH: A few overlapping evergreen branches can make a continuous garland. The stair rail is the fixed support that holds the greenery up.
notes.RIBBON: The ribbon can add color between the evergreen branches. A separate tie can hold the garland in place on the rail.

clues.BRANCH: Evergreen limb that can be tucked into a garland
clues.RIBBON: Decorative strip you can tie among evergreen branches

christmas-preparing-the-room-3.solvingTip: Look for the pointed decoration placed at the top of the tree at 5 Down. It shares a square with the name of the holiday at 7 Across.

clues.SILVER: Shiny gray color an ornament can have
clues.POINT: Part that sticks out from the center of a star ornament
clues.STAR: Pointed ornament placed at the top of a Christmas tree

notes.POINT: Each point sticks out from the center of the ornament. The tips give it the outline you see above the tree branches.
notes.BRANCH: The branches support the ornaments that hang lower on the tree. The star goes at the top, where the tree narrows to its highest point.
notes.CHRISTMAS: A star on a Christmas tree can recall the star in the Nativity story. Some homes use an angel or another ornament at the top instead.

christmas-preparing-the-room-4.solvingTip: Try the curved piece that holds the ornament to a branch at 1 Down. Its crossing names the small circle at the top of the ornament at 4 Across.

clues.LOOP: Small closed circle at the top of an ornament for hanging
clues.GLASS: Fragile material used for some shiny tree ornaments

notes.GLASS: A thin glass ornament can break if pressed against a hard object in the box. Tissue keeps the ornaments from knocking against one another.
notes.CHRISTMAS: When unpacking a Christmas bauble, look for the small loop at its top. A hook or ribbon goes through the loop to hang the ornament from a branch.

christmas-preparing-the-room-5.solvingTip: Find the part that covers one of the tiny houses at 9 Down. Its crossing names the route between rows of buildings at 8 Across.

notes.CHRISTMAS: In a tabletop Christmas village, several tiny buildings make one street scene. Place taller houses toward the back so smaller shops can be seen from the front of the mantel.
notes.HOUSE: A tiny house in the mantel scene can have a door, lit windows, and a pitched roof. The houses stand beside models of shops or other town buildings.

clues.CHRISTMAS: December holiday celebrated with miniature village displays
clues.HOUSE: Model of a home in a miniature holiday village

thanksgiving-small-moments.solvingTip: Start with the word that identifies the guest at 11 Across. Its crossing names the tool you use to write it at 10 Down.

notes.TABLE: A name card sits at each person's place on the table. Folding the card lets it stand up so the name is easier to read.
notes.PAPER: Choose paper stiff enough to hold a fold. A simple fold in the middle makes a small tent with a place for the name on the front.
notes.FAMILY: Several family members at Thanksgiving may share a last name. A first name or a familiar nickname on a place card makes it easier to find the right setting.

thanksgiving-small-moments-2.solvingTip: Try the word for good fortune at 7 Across. Its crossing names one of the parts a person holds after the bone breaks at 4 Down.

clues.FORK: Place where the turkey bone splits into two branches

notes.FORK: Each person holds one branch of the wishbone for the traditional pull. The fork is the place where those branches join.

thanksgiving-small-moments-3.solvingTip: Look for the curved shape of the harvest basket at 4 Across. Its crossing names the small fruit that grows in bunches at 3 Down.

notes.BASKET: A cornucopia is a basket shaped like a horn. It rests on its side so you can arrange fruit and nuts at its wide opening.
notes.TABLE: The Thanksgiving table holds both the meal and the decoration. A cornucopia can sit sideways in the center so its fruit and nuts show through the wide opening.

clues.BASKET: Woven container that can be shaped like a horn

thanksgiving-small-moments-4.solvingTip: Find the action that sends the football to a teammate at 5 Across. Its crossing names the number of points shown during the game at 6 Down.

clues.FIELD: Marked stretch of grass or turf where the game is played
clues.BALL: Oval object the players run with or throw
clues.GOAL: Word before line for the front edge of a football end zone

notes.SCORE: The numbers on the screen tell how many points each team has. The game clock shows how much time remains.

thanksgiving-small-moments-5.solvingTip: Try what holds the whole cheesecake in the oven at 1 Across. One crossing leads to the flat dish used to serve a slice at 1 Down.

clues.PAN: Metal container that holds the cheesecake while it bakes
clues.CHEESE: Cream ___, a main ingredient in the filling

notes.SWEET: Sugar makes the filling sweet, while cream cheese can give it a slight tang. The pumpkin and spice supply much of the flavor you smell as you take a bite.
notes.CHEESE: Cream cheese gives the cheesecake filling its soft, thick base. The pumpkin mixture is baked on the crust and firms up further as it cools.

garden-friendly-flowers.solvingTip: Picture what you would scoop around the pansy roots at 2 Down. Follow that crossing to the round dish on the front step at 5 Across.

clues.BOWL: Deep round dish that can hold a few pansies
clues.YELLOW: Bright color often seen near the middle of a pansy bloom

notes.COLOR: Purple and yellow can appear on the same pansy. In the bowl on the step, the blooms may repeat those hues in different combinations.
notes.YELLOW: On a pansy, a patch of yellow near the middle can stand out between dark markings that give the bloom a face-like look.
notes.PETAL: A pansy petal can have a dark patch or several fine lines pointing toward the middle. Those markings help give the bloom its face-like look.

garden-friendly-flowers-2.solvingTip: Look for the buzzing visitor that moves from one zinnia to the next at 7 Across. Its crossing asks what you planted before any flowers came up at 6 Down.

clues.ORANGE: Zinnia color between red and yellow

notes.COLOR: A zinnia's color is easiest to see on the small petals around the center. The green stalk can look much the same on a red flower and an orange one.
notes.PETAL: What looks like a zinnia petal is a broad part of a little flower along the edge. Several rows of those outer flowers can make a zinnia look very full.
notes.STEM: The green stem supports the zinnia flower. When you cut a few for a bunch, leaving some stem below each bloom gives you something to hold or put into a vase.

garden-friendly-flowers-3.solvingTip: Enter the yard through the movable part of the fence at 2 Across. Where it crosses 1 Down, picture one of the white pieces around a daisy's center.

notes.YELLOW: On a familiar white garden daisy, the yellow part is in the center and the white rays spread around it.
notes.WHITE: On many daisies, the parts we call white petals are the rays around a cluster of tiny flowers in the center.
notes.PETAL: The white rays of a daisy usually spread out from the center in a ring. As the bloom ages, they can droop while the yellow center remains on the stem.

clues.PETAL: One white part spreading outward from a daisy's center

garden-friendly-flowers-4.solvingTip: Think of the everyday object that gives an open spring flower its shape at 2 Down. The crossing at 4 Across asks for the flower itself.

garden-friendly-flowers-5.solvingTip: Imagine fastening a climbing stem loosely to its support at 10 Down. Use the crossing letter to name the shape of the leaves at 9 Across.

notes.FLOWER: Many familiar morning glories open early in the day. The open blue flower has a different shape from the heart-shaped leaves along the vine.
notes.SEED: A morning glory can start from a seed planted near a fence. As the young vine grows, its stem can wind around the support.
notes.FENCE: A morning glory can twine around the narrow parts of a fence. An open fence also leaves the leaves and flowers easy to see from either side.

clues.FENCE: Yard barrier a vine can climb

garden-cutting-table.solvingTip: Find what you would stand the cut flowers in at 12 Across. Then look at 11 Down for the part you'd shorten to make a flower sit lower.

notes.COLOR: A single snapdragon stalk can have open blossoms and unopened buds at the same time. Look at the open blossoms for the clearest view of their color.
notes.GLASS: In a clear glass vase, you can see the water line and the cut ends of the snapdragon stems. The taller blossoms and buds sit above the vase's narrow neck.

clues.GLASS: Clear material a tall vase can be made of

garden-cutting-table-2.solvingTip: Picture suspending the lavender upside down at 2 Down. Its crossing at 3 Across asks for a spot out of direct sunlight.

notes.STRING: The string keeps the lavender stems together as they dry. Leaving a loop above the knot gives you something to hang the bundle from.
notes.FLOWER: A lavender stem carries a cluster of tiny flowers near its tip. Those clusters can keep some of their scent after the cut stems have dried.
notes.DRAWER: A drawer is one place to put dried lavender after it has hung to dry. Keep the flowers in a small bag so loose pieces stay away from the folded clothes.

clues.DRAWER: Pull-out compartment where a bag of dried lavender may be kept

garden-cutting-table-3.solvingTip: At 4 Across, look for the lip that guides water when you pour. The crossing at 5 Down names the whole jug holding the hydrangeas.

notes.WHITE: Some hydrangeas have white clusters when they first open and develop a pink tint as the blooms age. The handled pitcher holds the whole cut stems.
notes.HANDLE: One hand can grip the loop on the side of the pitcher to carry it. The spout is the shaped lip on the opposite side.
notes.PORCH: The porch roof can shade the pitcher from strong sun. Set it where the flower clusters can be seen from the steps without getting in the way of the door.

clues.WHITE: Color of many hydrangea blooms when they first open

garden-cutting-table-4.solvingTip: Start with the wide-mouthed container on the table at 4 Down. At the crossing, 5 Across, fit the two-word name of the fragrant flowers it holds.

notes.WATER: The jar is a vase for ornamental sweet peas. The cut ends of the stems sit in water below the blossoms.
notes.PETAL: A sweet pea has a broad upper petal that can look like a tiny sail. Smaller petals cluster below it, giving the blossom its folded shape.

clues.WATER: Liquid that keeps cut stems fresh in a jar

garden-cutting-table-5.solvingTip: Find the place to sit near the peony at 3 Across. Then think of what you might notice in the air there at 2 Down.

notes.LEAF: A peony's green leaves grow along the stems below its round blooms. The leaves can still fill the space beside the seat after the flowers drop their petals.
notes.PETAL: Full peony blossoms may have several crowded layers of petals. Those layers make the center harder to see, even when the flower is open.

garden-flower-seasons.solvingTip: Start with the still water beside the iris at 8 Down. Follow the crossing toward the clue about one colorful part of a blossom at 8 Across.

clues.CLUMP: Group of stems growing close together
clues.GREEN: Color of the long leaves below an iris bloom

notes.GREEN: The upright leaves can stay green after the iris flowers fade. Their long shape makes the plant recognizable beside the pond even between blooms.
notes.PETAL: Many irises have three upright petals with three broader parts bending down around them. That gives the bloom a different outline when you look at it from the side.

garden-flower-seasons-2.solvingTip: Find the little building where you keep garden tools at 7 Down. Its crossing asks for the tall flower growing beside the wall at 8 Across.

notes.FLOWER: Hollyhock flowers line the tall stalk, and the lower ones often open first. From the side, you can see buds higher up above the open blooms.
notes.SUMMER: Hollyhocks can bloom along the shed wall in summer. Since the buds open over time, the same tall stalk can have both unopened buds and flowers.
notes.SEED: Hollyhock seeds can form in small round cases after the flowers fade. Collect them once those cases turn dry and brown.

clues.FLOWER: Bloom that opens along a hollyhock stalk
clues.SEED: Small part that can be saved from a dried flower head for planting

garden-flower-seasons-3.solvingTip: Imagine how those long flower stems move in a gentle wind at 6 Down. Use the crossing to name the warm season at 6 Across.

notes.FLOWER: What looks like one cosmos flower has many tiny flowers crowded into the center. The broad outer parts give the bloom its daisy-like shape.
notes.LIGHT: In this scene, light describes the force of the breeze. It is gentle enough to make the top of a cosmos stem sway a little.
notes.SUMMER: Cosmos can keep flowering through summer and into early fall. The flowers rise above fine leaves, so you can see them sway even when the lower foliage is still.

clues.LIGHT: Mild in force, as a gentle breeze

garden-flower-seasons-4.solvingTip: At 4 Across, find the part of the planter the petunias spill over. The crossing at 3 Down asks how the stems hang down its side.

notes.FLOWER: A petunia has a flared, trumpet-shaped flower at the end of a stem. On trailing kinds, several blooms can hang past the planter's rim.
notes.SUMMER: Trailing petunias can bloom through much of summer. As the stems grow past the rim, some flowers turn to face away from the sides of the planter.

garden-flower-seasons-5.solvingTip: Picture a snowdrop with its opening facing the ground at 5 Across. Name the ringing object it resembles, then cross into the clue for an open flower at 5 Down.

notes.WHITE: Look for the white hanging bloom above the snow or bare soil. Some snowdrops have small green marks on the inner parts of their flowers.
notes.GREEN: On a snowdrop, most of the bloom is white. Look closely toward the center and you may see small green marks above the hanging tips.

clues.WHITE: Usual color of a snowdrop flower

needle-and-thread-projects.solvingTip: Think of how you secure the end of a sewing thread at 1 Down. The crossing at 4 Across names the small fastener you're putting back on the sweater.

clues.SPARE: Extra button kept in case one falls off
clues.SCISSORS: Two-bladed tool used to trim sewing thread
clues.THREAD: Thin strand used to sew a button back on

notes.SCISSORS: Use scissors to cut a fresh length of sewing thread. After you tie the final knot behind the button, trim the loose end close to it.
notes.THREAD: Choose thread that blends with the button or the sweater. Passing it through the holes more than once can help hold the button in place.

needle-and-thread-projects-2.solvingTip: Look at the turned-under bottom of a curtain at 11 Down. Its crossing at 10 Across asks for the measurement you adjust by sewing it higher or lower.

notes.WINDOW: Measure from the curtain rod to where you want the bottom to sit near the window. The hem sets that lower edge after the fabric is folded under.
notes.THREAD: Thread can be chosen to match the curtain fabric so the hem is hard to see from the front. The stitches hold the turned edge in place.

clues.THREAD: Thin strand that can hold a curtain hem in place

needle-and-thread-projects-3.solvingTip: Picture the little curve of cord that slips over a fastener at 4 Down. Follow it to the round fastener itself at 6 Across.

notes.SCISSORS: Scissors cut the felt to size before it is folded. Rounded corners can be trimmed into the soft fabric before the case is stitched together.

needle-and-thread-projects-4.solvingTip: Start with a little piece left in the sewing basket at 3 Down. Its crossing at 7 Across asks what you could sew and stuff with a few of those pieces.

clues.PINCUSHION: Small stuffed pad that holds pins and needles
clues.COTTON: Plant fiber used in cloth scraps for a pincushion

notes.STITCH: Close stitches keep the stuffing from working through the edges of the pincushion. Small, evenly spaced loops can make the two fabric pieces sit smoothly together.
notes.THREAD: Sew around most of the pincushion and leave a gap for stuffing. Keeping enough thread on the needle lets you close that gap after the cushion is filled.

needle-and-thread-projects-5.solvingTip: Find the round frame that keeps the napkin flat while you sew at 10 Across. At the crossing, 6 Down names the material stretched inside it.

clues.CORNER: Point where two edges of a cloth napkin meet
clues.STITCH: One small pass of the needle in a sewn letter

notes.CORNER: A napkin corner is easy to spot even when the napkin is folded. Leave a little space between the initial and each of the two nearby edges.
notes.STITCH: Several short stitches placed end to end can trace the shape of a letter. The line can curve if you make the stitches shorter around the bend.

yarn-for-useful-things.solvingTip: Use the clue at 1 Down for making fabric with two needles. Where it crosses 5 Across, think of the band a different color of yarn makes.

yarn-for-useful-things-2.solvingTip: Start at the basin where the dishcloth will get used at 3 Across. Its crossing at 3 Down takes you back to the small loop you made with the hook.

clues.HOOK: Curved tool used to pull yarn through loops

yarn-for-useful-things-3.solvingTip: Think of the warm fiber that comes from sheep at 2 Across. Then use its crossing for the fluffy decoration you can make for the top of a hat at 1 Down.

yarn-for-useful-things-4.solvingTip: Imagine sitting down and spreading a blanket over your thighs at 9 Across. The crossing at 7 Down asks for one of the long tools used to make its loops.

clues.PATCH: Small piece of fabric sewn over a worn spot
clues.STITCH: One worked loop in a knitted row
clues.BLANKET: Soft knitted covering for your lap

notes.BLANKET: A lap blanket can be shorter and narrower than a bed blanket. That size lets it cover the thighs and knees while leaving the feet clear of most of the hanging cloth.

yarn-for-useful-things-5.solvingTip: Find the loose bit you would catch to start winding at 4 Across. Its crossing names the loose bundle you are unwinding at 2 Down.

paper-for-keepsakes.solvingTip: Think of what's waiting on your nightstand at 7 Down. The crossing at 7 Across asks for the card you can slip inside to find your place tomorrow.

notes.COLOR: The card stock and the tassel can be different colors. A tassel that shows up against the cover makes it easier to find the marker in a closed book.
notes.PAPER: Card stock is thicker than ordinary writing paper, so the finished bookmark stays fairly flat. A hole near one end leaves room for a tassel.

paper-for-keepsakes-2.solvingTip: Begin with the picture you took at a picnic at 3 Across. Where it crosses 1 Down, find the point where two edges of that picture meet.

notes.SCISSORS: Scissors can trim a caption or backing sheet to fit the scrapbook page. A printed copy of the picnic photo can be trimmed to fit the space above it.
notes.CORNER: Small paper photo corners can slip over the points of a picture. They hold the picture on the page while leaving the center clear.
notes.PHOTO: A scrapbook photo can sit next to a caption about the picnic. A date or park name adds details that may be hard to recognize later from the picture itself.

clues.SCISSORS: Tool with two blades for trimming scrapbook paper
clues.CORNER: Point where two edges of a photo meet
clues.PHOTO: Camera picture you can mount on a scrapbook page

paper-for-keepsakes-3.solvingTip: At 12 Across, look for the little label that tells who gets the present. Its crossing at 8 Down names what you can thread through the opening and tie.

clues.STAMP: Tool pressed in ink to print a small design

clues.STRING: Thin cord that passes through a gift tag's hole

paper-for-keepsakes-4.solvingTip: Think of the folded paper object you could wave on a hot day at 4 Across. The crossing at 1 Down takes you to the part you grip.

notes.COLOR: The paper's color still shows in the fold valleys. On a sheet printed on just one side, the reverse can also show when the fan is opened.
notes.HANDLE: The paper pleats open above the handle. The handle gives your fingers a place to grip without squeezing the wide part closed.

paper-for-keepsakes-5.solvingTip: Start with the container that keeps your mementos together at 4 Down. The crossing at 5 Across asks for a picture you might save in it.

notes.RIBBON: A strip of ribbon can make a border around the lid of the memory box. It can be glued down so the lid still lifts without untying anything.
notes.PAINT: Paint can go on the outside of the memory box and around its edges. Let the painted lid dry before closing it or attaching the decoration.
notes.LETTER: A saved letter can carry a memory in the writer's own words. Keeping a letter with a photo from the same occasion gives both items more context.

clues.LETTER: Handwritten message someone might save in a keepsake box

painting-home-projects.solvingTip: Start with the part that keeps rain out of the bird shelter at 7 Down. Where it crosses 8 Across, think of the material you cut into boards to build it.

clues.SAND: Smooth the wood by rubbing it with rough paper

painting-home-projects-2.solvingTip: Picture the top lip of a clay flower container at 9 Down. Use the crossing at 10 Across to name what you brush on to add color.

clues.SEAL: Coat the painted surface to keep moisture out
clues.PAINT: Colored coating a brush can put on a clay pot

painting-home-projects-3.solvingTip: Think about what the stones have to be before you can paint them at 3 Down. The crossing at 4 Across takes you back to washing off loose dirt with clean water.

clues.FLOWER: Blossom shape you might paint on a garden rock

painting-home-projects-4.solvingTip: Picture touching the brush lightly to the opening in a stencil at 7 Down. Where it crosses 9 Across, find the sticky strip that holds the stencil in place.

painting-home-projects-5.solvingTip: Find what you would apply with a wet brush at 9 Across. The crossing at 6 Down names the small handled object you're trying to capture on paper.

beads-and-ribbons.solvingTip: Look for the little pierced piece of jewelry at 8 Across. Its crossing at 4 Down names a fine strand you could pass through the opening.

beads-and-ribbons-2.solvingTip: Think of the decoration made by tying two loops at 9 Across. Use its crossing to work out the narrow piece of fabric they're made from at 6 Down.

beads-and-ribbons-4.solvingTip: Find the little decoration you slide onto a cord at 9 Across. The crossing at 7 Down asks for the opening the cord passes through.

clues.CORD: Thicker strand that can hold beads on a key ring

beads-and-ribbons-5.solvingTip: Find the soft container you're making at 10 Down. Its crossing at 9 Across asks for the narrow fabric strip that will make the carrying loop.

clues.THREAD: Thin strand used to sew a ribbon handle to cloth

notes.STITCH: Stitches across the ribbon end attach it to the cloth bag. A second row can share the pull when you lift the bag by the ribbon.

easy-woodwork-projects.solvingTip: Imagine what collects as you smooth the wood at 5 Across. The crossing at 6 Down takes you to the flat surface you're making to store things.

easy-woodwork-projects-2.solvingTip: Picture one wall of the wooden box at 1 Down. Where it crosses 4 Across, think of what extra water needs to do after you water the plants.

easy-woodwork-projects-4.solvingTip: At 2 Down, find the flat item with a raised edge. The crossing at 3 Across asks what its two handles help you do.

easy-woodwork-projects-5.solvingTip: Find the short pin that sticks out of a coat rack at 2 Down. At the crossing, 3 Across asks what you'd do with your coat when you come in.

quiet-table-hobbies.solvingTip: Think of the outside boundary you're assembling first at 8 Down. The crossing at 7 Across asks for one of the small parts that goes into it.

outdoor-hobby-bags.solvingTip: Find the long pencil mark you could make across the paper at 10 Across. The crossing at 9 Down takes you to the seat you might draw, or sit on, at the park.

clues.SHADE: Darken part of a drawing with a pencil
clues.PENCIL: Pointed drawing tool that can make erasable lines

notes.PENCIL: The pencil's point makes a narrow line for an edge in the sketch. Tilting the pencil can bring the side of the point against the paper for a wider mark.

outdoor-hobby-bags-2.solvingTip: At 10 Across, find the long pole you hold while fishing. Follow it to the crossing at 9 Down for the artificial bait you might tie onto the line.

clues.LINE: Thin cord that connects the rod to the bait
clues.HOOK: Curved pointed piece that catches a fish

outdoor-hobby-bags-3.solvingTip: Think of the protective holder for your binoculars at 8 Across. Where it crosses 4 Down, look for the kind of book you'd open to identify a bird.

notes.FEATHER: When a bird moves its wing, you may see feather markings that were tucked out of sight. Binoculars help you compare the shape and color of those marks.

outdoor-hobby-bags-4.solvingTip: Look for the transparent piece the light enters through at 11 Across. Its crossing at 6 Down takes you to the control you press when the flower is in view.

outdoor-hobby-bags-5.solvingTip: Find the toy you fly on a line at 1 Down. The crossing at 5 Across asks for the long strip trailing from it in the air.

clues.TAIL: Long strip trailing behind a kite
clues.STRING: Line you hold while a kite flies

notes.PAPER: The paper forms the light surface across the kite frame. The frame keeps that sheet stretched out so moving air can lift it.

collecting-family-stories.solvingTip: Picture turning a family photo over at 9 Across. Where it crosses 7 Down, think of the information tag you could attach so the names stay with the picture.

notes.LABEL: A photo label can record which person stands on which side of a group picture. The back of the print has room to write those details away from the image.
notes.PHOTO: Look at the people, clothes, or background of an old photo when placing it in order with others. A later label can record what you were able to work out.

collecting-family-stories-2.solvingTip: Start with the stiff slip you pull from the kitchen box at 1 Across. The crossing at 2 Down asks for the cooking directions written on it.

clues.FAMILY: Relatives who may pass recipes down through generations

notes.FAMILY: A family recipe book can hold dishes passed between generations. A note about who made a dish can keep part of its story with the instructions.

collecting-family-stories-3.solvingTip: Find the brief reminder you might write before an interview at 11 Across. At the crossing, 7 Down asks what to do while your grandparent is telling the story.

collecting-family-stories-4.solvingTip: Think of the word for your mother's or father's sister at 6 Across. It crosses 5 Down, the word for either your mother or your father.

collecting-family-stories-5.solvingTip: Find the metal container where the keepsakes are stored at 6 Across. The crossing at 3 Down asks for the mailed message you could unfold from inside it.

flower-and-fabric-crafts.solvingTip: At 11 Down, think of fastening the little bag shut with ribbon. The crossing at 10 Across asks what you notice when you open the drawer.

flower-and-fabric-crafts-2.solvingTip: Find the plant part you're laying between pages at 8 Down. Use its crossing at 9 Across to name one of the branching lines still visible after pressing.

clues.PAPER: Absorbent sheet material used to press leaves
clues.LEAF: Part of a plant you can press flat and dry between pages

flower-and-fabric-crafts-3.solvingTip: Look for the circular base of the wreath at 10 Across. The crossing at 7 Down asks for one narrow length of fabric you can tie onto it.

notes.COTTON: Cotton cloth can be cut into short strips for the wreath. Their cut edges may fray a little, giving the tied ring a softer look.
notes.SCISSORS: Fabric scissors let you cut along a line in cotton cloth. Narrow strips fit closer together as you tie them around the ring.

clues.SCISSORS: Tool with two blades for cutting cloth strips

flower-and-fabric-crafts-4.solvingTip: Think of the line where the pieces of the cushion cover meet at 3 Across. Its crossing at 3 Down asks for one small loop of thread along that line.

clues.THREAD: Fine strand used to sew the edges of a cushion cover together

flower-and-fabric-crafts-5.solvingTip: Picture securing the paper around the gathered stems at 4 Down. The crossing at 3 Across takes you back to what you did with the scissors to trim them.

notes.FLOWER: The bouquet is the whole group of cut flowers. One flower has its own head, with a stem below it to hold or trim.

bible-beginnings-2.solvingTip: Start with the name of the garden where Adam and Eve lived at 11 Across. The crossing at 9 Down asks for the kind of waterway that flowed out of it.

bible-beginnings-4.solvingTip: Picture the bird that brought a leaf back to Noah at 3 Down. Its crossing at 6 Across asks for the tree the leaf came from.

bible-beginnings-5.solvingTip: Find one of the building blocks used at Babel at 8 Down. Its crossing names the tall structure the people built with those blocks at 10 Across.

notes.SHADE: In Genesis, Abraham offers travelers a place to rest under a tree. The branches give them shade while food is prepared.

bible-family-journeys-2.solvingTip: Think of what Rebekah did to bring up a drink from the well at 2 Across. Where it crosses 1 Down, find what she gave the camels.

bible-family-journeys-4.solvingTip: Think of how Joseph was related to Jacob at 2 Across. Use that crossing to fill in the garment Jacob gave him at 1 Down.

bible-family-journeys-5.solvingTip: Start with the sturdy bag used to hold grain at 8 Down. The crossing at 9 Across asks for the unit of time in Joseph's prediction about plenty and shortage.

bible-moses-and-the-journey-2.solvingTip: Find the plant Moses saw burning at 9 Across. Its crossing at 10 Down asks how God described the ground where Moses stood.
